description: A version is proposed only once it has been public for two days, so that a release pulled or fixed in its first days never reaches a branch. internalChecksFilter is already strict by default; it is stated so that the wait is read here as holding back the branch and the pull request themselves, not only a status check on them

packageRules.description: The base image is pinned by digest, so that a tag such as debian:12 being pushed again with a rebuilt layer arrives as a pull request instead of slipping silently into the next build. Only the Dockerfile is pinned; the actions stay on their version tags

The official ubuntu image is proposed without the two-day wait. Docker Hub gives a tag's last push as its release time, and the official ubuntu tags are pushed again every day or two, so a tag would rarely look two days old and its updates would hardly ever be proposed. The image here is built on debian, not ubuntu; the rule is kept so that an ubuntu base added later does not fall into the same trap. Docker Hub names are matched as written, so each way of writing the image is listed. The pull request's checks still have to pass

Patch releases and digest updates, including the first pins, carry no intended change in behaviour, so they are merged by Renovate once the pull request's build has passed. The repository's own auto-merge is not used (platformAutomerge is off), and a pull request without passing checks is never merged. Minor and major updates are left open for review

Workflows are already read by the github-actions manager. Grouping them keeps a handful of actions from arriving as a handful of pull requests, since they are updated together and reviewed the same way
